verdict: The strategy uses future information. None of the performance numbers can be trusted until that is fixed.

1.title: Lookahead bias
1.finding: Weights change when future data is removed. On 2018-03-21 the QQQ weight is 1.000 with the full history but 0.000 when history stops at 2018-04-04 (3 of 12 cut dates show it). The strategy is reading the future.

2.title: Data leakage
2.finding: Replaced every price after two cut dates with random noise; no decision before the cut changed. Features, normalization and rankings only use past data.

3.title: Survivorship bias
3.finding: 0 of 1 names stopped trading during the sample, so some failures are included. Yahoo still has no fully delisted names, so this remains incomplete.

4.title: Multiple testing
4.finding: Against 1 variants you declared, a skill-less search would still find a Sharpe of about 0.00. Deflated Sharpe probability 1%; selection-adjusted Sharpe -0.51.

5.title: Overfitting
5.finding: 3 tunable parameter(s), 35 trades. Sharpe -0.49 before 2021-11-10 and -0.55 after. The later period doesn't hold up and/or the parameters sit on a narrow peak.

6.title: Out-of-sample contamination
6.finding: No out-of-sample start declared. Audition's own 70/30 split gives Sharpe -0.49 then -0.55, but if you saw that period while building the strategy it isn't out of sample. Declare oos_start and oos_looks.

7.title: Regime dependency
7.finding: No positive excess return overall, so no regime carries it.

8.title: Parameter sensitivity
8.finding: The base parameters lose money after costs (Sharpe -0.51); sensitivity is moot.

9.title: Sample size
9.finding: 4154 periods (16.5 years), 35 position openings, about 4154 independent observations. A Sharpe this size needs inf years to be 95% sure it beats zero. The sample is too small for the claimed statistics.

10.title: Statistical significance
10.finding: t-stat -2.08, probabilistic Sharpe 1%, block-bootstrap 95% interval for Sharpe -0.84 to -0.10. On 30 shuffled-calendar placebos (time structure destroyed) the strategy beat its real Sharpe 4 times, p = 0.16. The result is consistent with no edge.

11.title: Price adjustments
11.finding: Split- and dividend-adjusted prices; no split-sized jumps found (0 moves over 40% checked).

12.title: Historical constituents
12.finding: The universe is a fixed list for the whole history. Index membership at each date isn't reconstructed. For US large caps use UNIVERSE = "sp500".

13.title: Timestamp alignment
13.finding: Single venue, one daily calendar; signals and fills share timestamps.

14.title: Missing data
14.finding: Missing bars are rare (0.00%) and the strategy never holds through one.

15.title: Data revisions
15.finding: Signals on as-quoted prices give Sharpe -0.51 vs -0.51; back-adjustment doesn't drive the result. (Fundamental or estimate data, if any, isn't covered.)

16.title: Exchange calendars
16.finding: Exchange calendar is clean: no weekend rows, duplicates, holiday filler bars or long gaps.

17.title: Bad ticks
17.finding: No one-day spike-and-revert prints over 8 sigma.

18.title: Data source independence
18.finding: Only one data source (Yahoo) was used. Set APCA_API_KEY_ID / APCA_API_SECRET_KEY to have Audition cross-check US prices against Alpaca SIP data.

19.title: Fill assumptions
19.finding: All 70 fills happen at the next bar's open after the signal close, on bars that actually traded. No same-bar fills.

20.title: Slippage
20.finding: Slippage scales with each order's size and the asset's volatility (square-root impact model, coefficient 0.5), not a fixed number. Average all-in cost 1.8 bps per unit traded at $1,000,000.

21.title: Bid-ask spread
21.finding: Half the spread is paid on every trade. Each asset's spread is the typical quoted spread for its dollar volume over the last two years, or a high/low estimate (Abdi-Ranaldo) for names under $2M a day, floor 1 bps: QQQ 1.0 bps ($25,597M/day). Declare DECLARE['costs'] = {'spread_bps': ..} to use your broker's numbers.

22.title: Partial fills
22.finding: Orders stay under 0.03% of daily volume (95th pct); full fills at the open are plausible.

23.title: Market impact
23.finding: Median order is 0.007% of 20-day dollar volume (95th pct 0.03%). Impact moves Sharpe from -0.51 to -0.51 at $1,000,000.

24.title: Latency
24.finding: Sharpe -0.61 if filled at the signal's own close (impossible), -0.51 at the next open (Audition default), -0.45 one day later.

27.title: Order execution
27.finding: Market-on-open orders, filled at the actual open including overnight gaps; no intrabar assumptions.

28.title: Capacity
28.finding: Sharpe by capital: $0.1M -0.51, $1M -0.51, $10M -0.53, $100M -0.57, $1000M -0.69. Keeps half its small-account Sharpe up to about $0M.

29.title: CAGR calculation
29.finding: You reported CAGR 31.0%; Audition measures -1.3% over the same window. CAGR -1.3%, compounded daily, net of all costs, idle cash earning T-bills (-2.7% if idle cash earned nothing). The reported number doesn't reproduce.

30.title: Sharpe calculation
30.finding: You reported Sharpe 2.10; Audition measures -0.51 over the same window. Sharpe -0.51 on daily excess returns over 13-week T-bills, annualized by sqrt(252). Ignoring the risk-free rate would show -0.23.

31.title: Serial correlation
31.finding: Lag-1 autocorrelation -0.143. Autocorrelation-adjusted Sharpe (Lo 2002) -0.54 vs -0.51 naive; from monthly returns -0.58.

32.title: Maximum drawdown
32.finding: You reported max drawdown -9.0%; Audition measures -36.0% over the same window. Max drawdown -36.0% on daily net equity; Calmar -0.04.

33.title: Drawdown duration
33.finding: Longest time under water: 4151 periods (16.5 years).

34.title: Tail risk
34.finding: Worst day -5.8%, worst month -9.4%, expected shortfall -0.40% (95%) / -2.32% (99%) per day, skew -4.53, excess kurtosis 132.5. Fat left tail: the average hides occasional large losses.

35.title: Leverage
35.finding: Gross exposure averages 0.03x, peaks at 1.00x. Leverage is financed at T-bills + 0.5% and included in every return and risk figure.

36.title: Concentration
36.finding: Single-asset strategy; concentration is by design.

37.title: Correlation
37.finding: Average pairwise correlation of held assets n/a; about 1.0 effective positions at a time.

38.title: Benchmark comparison
38.finding: Against buy-and-hold SPY (Sharpe 0.78, CAGR 13.8%): beta 0.08, alpha -3.7%/yr, alpha t-stat -2.97. Holding the index did better on a risk-adjusted basis.

39.title: Resampling methodology
39.finding: Stationary block bootstrap (mean block 20 periods) keeps volatility clustering and autocorrelation. Median 3-year max drawdown -8.1% with blocks vs -9.4% if days were shuffled independently.

40.title: Tail distributions
40.finding: Resampling can't produce a day worse than the worst one in the sample (-5.8%). 5th-percentile 3-year drawdown is -22.5%; a crash larger than anything in the data isn't in these numbers.

41.title: Parameter uncertainty
41.finding: Across 38 plausible parameter sets, Sharpe ranges -0.85 to -0.39 (5th-95th pct), CAGR -4.8% to -0.3%.

42.title: Cost stress testing
42.finding: Sharpe at 0x costs -0.50, 1x costs -0.51, 2x costs -0.53, 3x costs -0.54, 5x costs -0.57. Doubling costs wipes out the edge.

43.title: Regime changes
43.finding: Resampling only bear-market periods (603 of them): 68% chance of losing money over a year, median drawdown -8.5%.

44.title: Sample independence
44.finding: Paths are resampled from 4154 periods (4154 effectively independent); confidence intervals use the real sample length, not the number of paths.

45.title: Ruin probability
45.finding: Over 3 years: 3.0% chance of a 25% drawdown, 0.0% chance of 50%, 61.6% chance of ending down.

46.title: Shared tool dependency
46.finding: Audition is a separate engine from whatever produced your backtest, but it uses Yahoo data, so a shared data error isn't ruled out.

47.title: Shared specifications
47.finding: Process question: have someone write the rules from the idea, not from your spec or code.

48.title: Independent calculations
48.finding: Every return, cost and statistic here was recomputed by Audition from the strategy's raw target weights; none came from the strategy's own code or tool.

49.title: Implementation equivalence
49.finding: Your numbers don't reproduce: cagr reported 0.31 vs Audition -0.013; sharpe reported 2.1 vs Audition -0.513; max_dd reported -0.09 vs Audition -0.36. The original implementation differs from the rules in this file, or its accounting is off.

50.title: Reproducibility
50.finding: A manifest with the strategy hash, data fingerprint, parameters, seeds and versions is saved with this report.

51.title: Numerical accuracy
51.finding: Re-running in 32-bit floats moves Sharpe by 0.0000; numeric precision doesn't matter here.

52.title: Independent verification
52.finding: This run is an independent verification: Audition's data, fills, costs and statistics share no code with the tool the strategy was developed in.

53.title: Forward performance
53.finding: No forward results. At this Sharpe, about inf years of live or paper trading are needed to confirm it with 95% confidence.

54.title: Paper/live discrepancy
54.finding: Outside a backtest. Compare paper fills to real fills once trading.

55.title: Execution reliability
55.finding: Outside a backtest. Needs a live log of signals vs orders vs positions.

56.title: Risk controls
56.finding: No risk controls declared (position limit, daily loss limit, kill switch).

57.title: Data outages
57.finding: Survived a simulated 5-day data blackout without errors or exposure spikes. Live feeds fail in other ways too (stale prices, bad ticks), so test the live system.

58.title: Strategy degradation
58.finding: Suggested tripwire: a live 6-month Sharpe below nan happens in only 5% of 6-month stretches of the backtest itself, so treat it as a sign the edge has decayed. Six months is noisy: the backtest's own range is that wide. Last 6 months in sample: 0.00.

59.title: Capital allocation
59.finding: Your call. For sizing: annual vol 5.2%, max drawdown -36.0%, 3-year 50% drawdown odds in the Monte Carlo section.

60.title: Operational resilience
60.finding: Outside a backtest. Needs restart, API-failure and rejected-order drills on the live system.

61.title: Turnover and holding period
61.finding: Trades 4.2x its capital a year; a position is held about 3 periods on average. Costs scale with this.

62.title: Cross-market replication
62.finding: Only one market was run. Add --regions to replay the file elsewhere.

63.title: Rolling stability
63.finding: Rolling one-year Sharpe is positive 16% of the time (range -1.92 to 1.51).

64.title: Timing luck
64.finding: Sharpe trading 1-5 days after the signal: -0.51, -0.45, -0.59, -0.66, -0.89. Spread 0.44.

65.title: Start-date sensitivity
65.finding: Starting in any year from 2010 to 2024: Sharpe -0.61 to 0.07, CAGR -1.7% to 4.6%. Negative from 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013.

66.title: Universe sensitivity
66.finding: Only 1 assets; too few to subsample.

67.title: Best-day dependence
67.finding: CAGR -1.3%; without its 10 best days (0.24% of the sample) -3.1%. T-bills returned 1.5%.

68.title: Own-universe benchmark
68.finding: Equal-weighting every asset in the same universe (no costs) gives Sharpe 0.85, CAGR 18.3%; the strategy gives -0.51 and -1.3% after costs.

69.title: Win/loss profile
69.finding: 35 positions: 29% winners, profit factor 0.28, average win 0.69x the average loss. Best position 5.03% of equity, worst -7.53%.

70.title: Drawdown pain
70.finding: Ulcer index 18.2%; more than 10% below the high 92% of the time; recovery factor (total return / max drawdown) -0.5.

71.title: Factor attribution
71.finding: Against the Fama-French five factors plus momentum (weekly, 2010-04-30 to 2026-10-02, Newey-West): alpha -3.5%/yr (t -2.54), R² 0.04. Main exposures: Mkt-RF +0.06 (t 2.5), RMW +0.04 (t 1.3), CMA -0.04 (t -0.8). No alpha after factors: a factor ETF mix would have done the same job.

events.verdict: Positions held through month turns gave back 16% of gross P&L on 20% of exposure. Strip every event and the Sharpe drops from -0.51 to -0.63: much of this strategy is an event bet, whether or not it was designed as one.

twins.verdict: Nothing in the library explains it well (best mix R² 6%, closest twin S&P 500 at 0.24). Original, or noise; the other tapes decide which. What's left after the twins: alpha -3.5% a year (t -2.5), Sharpe -0.71 versus -0.52 in total.
